title: Longest Alternating Subarray
summary: Given an integer array nums, find the longest subarray where elements alternate between increasing by 1 and decreasing by 1.
statement: Given an integer array nums, find the longest subarray where elements alternate between increasing by 1 and decreasing by 1. The subarray must be at least two elements long. If no such subarray exists, return -1. A subarray is a continuous segment of the original array.
constraints: A qualifying subarray has length at least two.
Its consecutive differences must be +1,-1,+1,-1 and so on, beginning with +1.
Return the maximum length, or -1 when none exists.
hints: A +1 step starts length two or extends only after an odd-length suffix; a -1 step extends only after even length.
Reset otherwise and record lengths at least two.
The expected next sign is determined entirely by suffix parity, so the recurrence preserves exactly the longest valid ending here.
editorial: The expected next sign is determined entirely by suffix parity, so the recurrence preserves exactly the longest valid ending here.

tests.explanation: The suffix 3,4,3,4 has differences +1,-1,+1 and length four.
No adjacent pair begins with a +1 difference, so return -1.
